Demography.question: 1) Demography is the scientific study of:
Demography.exp: Demography deals with human population. It studies size, structure, distribution and changes in population. It is closely related to fertility, mortality and migration.

Demography.question: 2) The major data provider for demography is:
Demography.exp: Census is the major data provider for population study. It gives information about population size and composition. Other agencies may also contribute demographic data.

Demography.question: 3) Census is mainly concerned with:
Demography.exp: Census counts the population of a country or area. It also records demographic characteristics. It is essential for planning health and social services.

Demography.question: 4) Which is a demographic process?
Demography.exp: Fertility is one of the demographic processes. It affects population growth through births. Mortality, marriage, migration and social mobility are also included.

Demography.question: 5) Which is not listed as a demographic process?
Demography.exp: Morbidity is disease frequency, not a demographic process in this classification. Demographic processes include fertility and mortality. Marriage, migration and social mobility are also included.

Demography.question: 6) Marriage is considered a:
Demography.exp: Marriage is included among demographic processes. It influences fertility and family formation. It indirectly affects population growth.

Demography.question: 7) Social mobility means movement mainly in:
Demography.exp: Social mobility refers to movement within social hierarchy. It may be upward or downward. It is included among demographic processes.

Demography.question: 8) Migration means:
Demography.option3: Movement of people from one place to another
Demography.exp: Migration changes population size and distribution. It may be internal or international. It is a major demographic process.

Demography.question: 9) High stationary stage has:
Demography.option1: Low birth rate and high death rate
Demography.option2: High birth rate and low death rate
Demography.option3: Low birth rate and low death rate
Demography.option4: High birth rate and high death rate
Demography.exp: High stationary stage has both high birth and death rates. Population growth is usually slow. It represents a pre-transition pattern.

Demography.question: 10) Early expanding stage is characterized by:
Demography.option1: Low birth rate and low death rate
Demography.option2: High birth rate with beginning decline in death rate
Demography.option3: Birth rate lower than death rate
Demography.option4: Falling birth rate and high death rate
Demography.exp: In early expanding stage, birth rate remains high. Death rate begins to decline. This leads to population growth.

Demography.question: 11) Late expanding stage shows:
Demography.option1: Birth rate tends to fall and death rate declines further
Demography.option2: Both birth and death rates very high
Demography.option3: Birth rate lower than death rate
Demography.option4: Death rate higher than birth rate
Demography.exp: Late expanding stage has falling birth rate. Death rate continues to decline further. Bangladesh is placed in this stage in the notes.

Demography.question: 12) Low stationary stage has:
Demography.option1: Low birth and low death rates
Demography.option2: Falling birth and falling death rates
Demography.option3: High birth and high death rates
Demography.option4: High birth and falling death rates
Demography.exp: Low stationary stage has both low birth and death rates. Population growth becomes slow and stable. Several developed countries are examples.

Demography.question: 13) Declining stage is characterized by:
Demography.option1: Death rate continuously falling below zero
Demography.option2: Birth rate higher than death rate
Demography.option3: Both birth and death rates high
Demography.option4: Birth rate lower than death rate
Demography.exp: In declining stage, birth rate is lower than death rate. Population may decrease naturally. Germany and Hungary are given as examples.

Demography.question: 14) African countries are mentioned as examples of:
Demography.exp: African countries are given as examples of early expanding stage. In this stage birth rate remains high. Death rate begins to decline.

Demography.question: 15) Bangladesh is placed in which demographic cycle stage?
Demography.exp: Bangladesh is listed under late expanding stage. Birth rate tends to fall. Death rate declines further.

Demography.question: 16) India, China and Singapore are also examples of:
Demography.exp: India, China and Singapore are grouped with Bangladesh. They are examples of late expanding stage. This stage shows falling birth rate with further death rate decline.

Demography.question: 17) UK, Denmark, Sweden and Belgium are examples of:
Demography.exp: These countries are examples of low stationary stage. Both birth and death rates are low. Population growth is usually slow.

Demography.question: 18) Germany and Hungary are examples of:
Demography.exp: Germany and Hungary are examples of declining stage. Birth rate is lower than death rate. Natural population growth becomes negative.

Demography.question: 19) Pre-transition pattern is best represented by:
Demography.exp: High stationary stage represents the pre-transition pattern. Both birth and death rates are high. Population size remains relatively static.

Demography.question: 20) Age-sex pyramid is a graphic representation of:
Demography.option3: Age and sex distribution of population
Demography.exp: Age-sex pyramid shows age and sex structure. It displays population distribution by age groups. It also separates males and females.

Demography.question: 21) In an age-sex pyramid, males are usually shown on the:
Demography.exp: In a population pyramid, males are shown on the left. Females are shown on the right. Age groups are arranged vertically.

Demography.question: 22) In an age-sex pyramid, females are usually shown on the:
Demography.exp: Females are shown on the right side of the pyramid. Males are shown on the left. This makes sex comparison easy across age groups.

Demography.question: 23) Developing countries like Bangladesh usually have which type of age-sex pyramid?
Demography.exp: Bangladesh has an expansive population pyramid. It has a broad base. This reflects high child population and high birth rate.

Demography.question: 24) A broad-based population pyramid suggests:
Demography.option2: High child population and high birth rate
Demography.exp: Broad base means many children in the population. It usually indicates high birth rate. This pattern is common in developing countries.

Demography.question: 25) Developed countries like the UK usually show:
Demography.exp: Developed countries commonly show stationary or constrictive pyramids. The base is narrow. There may be a bulge in the middle age groups.

Demography.question: 26) A narrow base in a population pyramid indicates:
Demography.exp: A narrow base means fewer children are being born. This suggests low fertility or low birth rate. It is common in developed or ageing populations.

Demography.question: 27) Bulge in the middle of age-sex pyramid indicates:
Demography.exp: A middle bulge suggests many middle-aged people. It is commonly seen in stationary or constrictive pyramids. It often reflects lower fertility and longer survival.

Demography.question: 28) Which pair is correctly matched?
Demography.option1: High stationary — low birth and low death rate
Demography.option2: Declining — high birth and high death rate
Demography.option3: Late expanding — birth rate tends to fall
Demography.option4: Early expanding — birth rate lower than death rate
Demography.exp: Late expanding stage has falling birth rate. Death rate declines further. Bangladesh is an example of this stage.

Demography.question: 29) Which stage has the fastest population growth tendency?
Demography.exp: Early expanding stage has high birth rate with falling death rate. This creates rapid natural increase. The gap between births and deaths becomes wide.

Demography.question: 30) Which demographic stage is most associated with ageing population?
Demography.exp: Low birth rate reduces the proportion of children. Longer survival increases older age groups. This produces an ageing population pattern.

Demography.question: 31) Which country pair is matched with declining stage?
Demography.exp: Germany and Hungary are examples of declining stage. In this stage birth rate is lower than death rate. Population may decrease without immigration.

Demography.question: 32) Which country pair is matched with low stationary stage?
Demography.exp: UK and Denmark are examples of low stationary stage. Both birth and death rates are low. Sweden and Belgium are also examples.

Demography.question: 33) Which feature best fits Bangladesh’s age-sex pyramid?
Demography.exp: Bangladesh has an expansive age-sex pyramid. It has a broad base. This indicates high child population and high birth rate.

Demography.question: 34) Population pyramid is useful mainly for planning:
Demography.exp: Population pyramid shows age and sex composition. It helps estimate needs for child health, schools, reproductive health and elderly care. It also helps predict future dependency burden. Health planning becomes more realistic when age structure is known.

Demography.question: 35) Dependency ratio compares dependent age groups with:
Demography.exp: Dependency ratio compares children and elderly with working-age people. It reflects the economic burden on productive age groups. High dependency ratio means fewer workers support more dependents. It is important for social and health service planning.

Demography.question: 36) A population with many children will mainly have high:
Demography.exp: A broad base means many children. This increases child dependency ratio. Such populations need more maternal, child health and education services. Developing countries commonly show this pattern.

Demography.question: 37) Sex ratio usually expresses the number of:
Demography.exp: In standard demographic use, sex ratio is often expressed as number of females per 100 males in many public health texts. Some countries may express it differently, so wording of the question matters. It describes sex composition of population. It helps identify imbalance due to migration, mortality or social factors.

Demography.question: 38) Crude birth rate is calculated as live births in a year per:
Demography.exp: Crude birth rate measures live births in a year per 1,000 mid-year population. It is called crude because the denominator includes all ages and both sexes. It is simple and widely used. But it is affected by age-sex structure of the population.

Demography.question: 39) Crude death rate is calculated as deaths in a year per:
Demography.exp: Crude death rate measures total deaths in a year per 1,000 mid-year population. It gives an overall idea of mortality in a community. It is crude because it does not adjust for age structure. An older population may show higher crude death rate even with good health care.

Demography.question: 40) Natural growth rate of population mainly depends on:
Demography.exp: Natural growth depends on births and deaths. Migration changes population size but is not part of natural increase. When births exceed deaths, population increases naturally. When deaths exceed births, population declines naturally.
